chapters.title_en: The Elegant Refutation of the Divinity of Jesus by the Clear Text of the Gospel — Section 1: On the Weak Foundations of Christian Doctrinal Inquiry and the Two Classes of Adherents
chapters.arabic_text:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم- وبه ثقتي:
أما بعد حمد الله، والصلاة على محمد خير خلقه وآله، فإني رأيت مباحث
النصارى «1» المتعلقة بعقائدهم؛ ضعيفة المباني، واهية القوى، وعرة المسالك،
يقضي المتأمل من عقول جنحت إليها غاية عجبه، ولا يقف من تعقيدها على اليسير
من إربه، لا يعولون فيها إلا على التقليد المحض، عاضين [بالنواجذ] على
ظواهر أطلقها الأولون، ولم ينهض بإيضاح مشكلها- لقصورهم- الآخرون، ظانين
بأن ذلك هو الشرع الذي شرعه لهم عيسى عليه السلام، معتذرين عن اعتقادها/
بما ورد من نصوص يعتقدون أنها قاهرة للكفر، غير قابلة للتأويل «2»، وأن
صرفها عن ظواهرها عسيرة «3». وهم في ذلك طائفتان:
- طائفة- وهم الأكثر- لم يمارسوا شيئا من العلوم التي يقف بها الناظر على
استحالة المستحيل، فيجزم باستحالة وجوده، وإيجاب الواجب، فينفي عدم وقوعه
وإمكان الممكن، فلا محالا لازما لطرفي وجوده وعدمه، بل PageV01P025
ارتسمت في أذهانهم صور منذ صغرهم، واستمرت بهم الغباوة «1» إلى أن صار ذلك
فيهم ملكة.
فهذه الطائفة برؤها من دائها عسير/.
وطائفة لهم أدنى معقول، وقد ألموا بيسير من العلوم، فتجدهم ناكصين عن هذا
المعتقد، لا يسامحون أفكارهم بمقاربته، يعولون تارة على تقليد الفيلسوف «2»
في مسألة الاتحاد لإعظامهم ما يؤدي إليه من هدم قواعد تظافر على ثبوتها
صرائح العقول، فارين من هذه المعضلة إلى التقليد المحض، معتقدين أن
الفيلسوف قد حاول العلوم الخفية، فأبانها جلية مبرهنة. ظانين بأن من هذا
شأنه جدير بأن يعول على أقواله، وتقلد «3» في المعتقدات! فلذلك ينفصلون عن
مسألة الاتحاد «4» بردها إلى مسألة تعلق النفس بالجسد/.
ولو راجع هؤلاء المساكين عقولهم وتركوا الهوى والتعصب، لعلموا أنهم قد
نكبوا عن محجة الصواب، وأخطئوا سبيل الحق لوجوه:
أحدها: أنهم إن جعلوا ذلك من قبيل القياس، فغلط، لأن القياس «5»:
«رد فرع إلى أصل بعلة جامعة هي مناط الحكم».
PageV01P026
وأي علة عقلها هذا القائل مقتضية لحقيقة التعلق الذي يقول به الفيلسوف، ثم
بعد ذلك يعديها إلى ذات الباري «1» ليصح له القياس.
وإن جعل ذلك من قبيل التشبيه والتمثيل «2» فغلط أيضا، لأن المشبه به لا
بد أن  يكون/ معلوما متصورا حتى يكون العلم به مقتضيا للعلم بالمشابهة.
والقائل منهم «3» بهذه المقالة لو بذل جهده على أن يأتي بأدنى شبهة تقفه
على حقيقة النفس، وحقيقة التعلق، القائل بهما الفيلسوف، لأقر بالعجز عن
إدراك ذلك، فكيف يصح له القياس والحقائق غير معلومة له؟!
ثم إن مثل هذا القياس لا يسامح الفروعي نفسه في استعماله، بل هو من
الأقيسة [المهجورة] «4»، المسمى بقياس التعقيد، وهو أن يحاول إثبات حكم
خفي، فيثبته بما هو أخفى منه، أو بما يحتاج في إثباته إلى إعمال الفكر
واستخراجه/ بالأدلة الغامضة، كالنفس، القائل بها الفيلسوف، التي لا يتخيل
وجودها إلا بتعقيدات وغموض في المأخذ، وإذا كان هذا «5» مهجورا في الفروع
المبنية على أيسر ظن، فكيف يعول عليه في الأصول المتعلقة PageV01P027
بذات واجب الوجود «1»؟! وكيف يتم ادعاء ذلك، ومناط الحكم لو عثر عليه،
لاقتضى أن لا يكون للإله تعلق بذات أحد من البشر على حد تعلق النفس بالبدن،
لأنهم يقولون: إن كل نفس تعلقت ببدن فشرط تعلقها به أن يكون بينها وبينه
مناسبة وملاءمة، لأجلها كان التعلق.
والإله- جل اسمه- منزه عن مثل ذلك/. ثم لو سلم لهم ذلك، وأن التعلق الذي
حاولوه متصور على وفق الآراء الفلسفية، لم يحصل لهم به غناء ولم ينهض ذلك
بمقصودهم في إثباتهم الإلهية لعيسى عليه السلام.
لأن الفيلسوف يقول: إن للنفس بالبدن تعلقا تدبيريا، وأن اللذة والألم
يحصلان لهما بواسطة تعلقها به، إذا انفعلت القوة الحساسة بالملائم
والمنافي، ومحال أن يراد هذا التعلق بجملته مع ما ذكر، لأن حصول اللذات
لذات الباري محال.
بقي أن تؤخذ هذه النسبة التدبيرية مجردة عن حصول اللذات، وهذا أيضا غير
مجد، لأن الخالق مدبر/ لكل فرد من أفراد العالم، وله إلى كل مخلوق نسبة
تدبيرية.
فإن قيل: المراد نسبة ظهر أثرها في خرق العوائد؛ كإحياء الميت وغير ذلك،
فيدل إذ ذاك على المقصود.
فالجواب: أن مثل هذه النسبة التي يتمكن المتصف بها من الإتيان بخرق
العوائد، ثابتة لغير عيسى عليه السلام، فإنهم معترفون بأن موسى عليه  السلام
قلب العصا ثعبانا.
وهل إحياء الميت إلا عبارة عن اتصاف الجماد بالحيوانية؟
بل هذا أدل على المعجز «2»، لأن جعل ما لم يتصف بالحياة قط حيا؛ PageV01P028
أدل على القدرة من إعادة الشيء إلى حالته الأولى/. ثم انشقاق البحر وجعل كل
فرق كالطود العظيم، من غرائب المعجزات.
وقد شهدت التوراة التي يصدقونها بأن موسى عليه السلام أخرج يده برصاء
كالثلج، ثم أعادها إلى لون جسده.
وفي أسفار الملوك والقضاة، وهو من جملة كتبهم العتيقة التي تقرأ في
كنائسهم، أن إيليا واليشع تلميذه أقاما الميت، وإحياء إيليا لابن الأرملة
عندهم غير منكور، ووقوف الشمس أيضا ليوشع إلى أن أخذ المدينة- أريحا- من
بدائع المعجزات.
ثم لما من الأنبياء؛ أنبياء لم ترسل «1»، فما المانع أن تكون هذه النسبة
ثابتة/ لكل واحد منهم، لكنها لم تظهر لعدم الرسالة المحوجة إلى البراهين
الصادرة عنها؟!
دقيقة يجب التنبيه عليها:
لفظ الكتاب العزيز: واضمم يدك إلى جناحك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء «2»، ولفظ
التوراة: «وهنا يا ذو مصورا عث كالشولغ».
وتفسير هذا اللفظ العبراني بالعربية: «وهذه يدك برصاء كالثلج».
صرحت التوراة «3» بالبرص، وصريح الكتاب العزيز بأن بياضها من غير PageV01P029
سوء، وفي القلب حسيكة «1» من ذلك في بادئ الرأي، لكن الجمع على الممارس
الفهم غير عسير.
وبيانه: أن البرص/ عبارة عن عرض ينشأ عن سوء مزاج يحصل بسببه تلزج بلغم
تضعف القوة المغيرة عن إحالته إلى لون الجسد.
ومعلوم أن بياض يد موسى عليه السلام ما نشأ عن سوء مزاج، لأن كل أحد إذا
ساء مزاجه على نهج ما وصفناه، حصل له ذلك، وإذا قويت القوة المغيرة إحالته،
فحينئذ تذهب خصوصية الإعجاز. بل بياضها كان من قبيل المعجز الخارق.
وشأن المعجز الخارق أن يكون مخالفا للمعهود المألوف، وإلى هذا المعنى
إشارة الكتاب العزيز بقوله: من غير سوء. أي أن الله أقدر موسى على أن/ يجعل
يده برصاء من غير سوء، وأن يردها إلى لون جسده، من غير قوة مغيرة، ليحصل له
بذلك خصوصية بإجراء المعجز الخارق المخالف للمعهود على يده.
وإنما يكون معجزا مخالفا للمعهود؛ إذا أتى بالمسبب منفكا عن سببه العادي،
الذي لا ينشأ إلا عنه، ثم عبر عنه بالبياض الذي هو من لوازمه، هذا جمع واضح.
ومما يوهي معتقداتهم في هذه المسألة؛ أن قاعدة الفيلسوف في النفس
وتعلقها، إن كانوا جازمين بثبوتها، ومستند جزمهم حسن الظن بالقائلين بها،
وهم غير قادرين على الإتيان/ ببراهينها، ظنا منهم أن القائلين بها قد
اخترعوا من العلوم الخفية، ما يرجع الفكر ناكصا عن إدراكها، لخفاء مأخذها
وصعوبة مبانيها.
وأن من هذا شأنه تكون أقواله مبرأة من الخطأ، فيجب على هذا القائل أن
يقلد الفيلسوف في أن النبوات مكتسبة، وأن العالم قديم لا يقبل الكون
والفساد، وأن الباري لا يعلم الجزئيات، وأن الواحد لا يصدر عنه إلا واحد،
وأن إله الخلق وجود مجرد، لم يقم بذاته علم ولا حياة ولا قدرة، إلى غير PageV01P030
ذلك مما نقضوا به قواعد المتشرعين وصرحوا فيه بإكذاب الأنبياء «1» /
المرسلين.
ومن العجب تقليدهم قوما يمنعون تصور ما يثبت به خصوصية صاحب شرعهم لنصهم
على استحالة انعقاد الولد من محض مني أمه من غير مشاركة مني رجل، إما عاقد
على رأي كبيرهم، أو مشارك له في الجزئية على رأي جالينوس «2».
فإن حمل قائلا تعصبه وهواه المحرضان له على عدم تركه ما ألفه؛ قائلا: إن
ما ذكر قامت البراهين على خطئهم فيه، فتبقى فيما وراءه على مقتضى ظننا بهم.
فالجواب: أن من ظهر تارة خطؤه، وتارة صوابه، كانت أقواله ممكنة الخطإ/
والصواب، ولا يصار إلى تقليد من هذا شأنه مع عدم الوقوف على مستند أقواله،
ونبذ أقوال المتشرعين وراء ظهره، وعدم التفاته إلى التعويل على ظواهر كتابه
الدالة على إنسانية صاحب شريعته إلا لنصوص أبت التأويل «3» دالة على ما
يدعونه من الإلهية، مستعصية على العقول استعصاء بينا. كيف وفي الإنجيل «4»
نصوص مصرحة PageV01P031
بإنسانية عيسى عليه السلام «1» المحضة، ونصوص شاهدة بأن إطلاق الإلهية
عليه، على ما يدعون محال.
وهذه النصوص في أصح الأناجيل/ عندهم؛ إنجيل يوحنا بن زبدا «2».
وها أنا أذكر نصا،  نصا، مبينا فصولها المسطرة فيه حذرا من المناكرة، لأن
كتبهم غير محفوظة في صدورهم.
وقبل الشروع في ذكرها؛ فلا بد من تقديم أصلين متفق عليهما بين أهل العلم؛
أحدهما: أن النصوص إذا وردت؛ فإن وافقت المعقول؛ تركت ظواهرها، وإن خالفت
صريح المعقول؛ وجب تأويلها واعتقاد أن حقائقها ليست مرادة، فيجب إذ ذاك
ردها إلى المجاز «3».
PageV01P032
الثاني: أن الدلائل إذا تعارضت فدل بعضها على إثبات حكم وبعضها PageV01P033
على نفيه، فلا نتركها/ متعارضة إلا وقد أحسسنا من أنفسنا العجز باستحالة PageV01P034
إمكان الجمع، وامتناع جعلها متظافرة على معنى واحد.
PageV01P035
وإذا تقرر ذلك، فلنشرع الآن في ذكر النصوص الدالة على التجوز في إطلاقه ما
يوهم الإلهية على نفسه.
PageV01P036
والنصوص الدالة على التجوز في مسألة الاتحاد «1»؛ كقوله:
PageV01P037
«أنا والأب واحد، ومن رآني فقد رأى الأب، وأنا في الأب، والأب في» «1».
ثم نتبع ذلك بذكر النصوص الدالة على إنسانيته المحضة، ونجمع بينها وبين
النصوص المثيرة لهم شبها نكصت أفهامهم لقصورها عن تأويلها، فعموا وضلوا.
بالغين/ في إيضاحها، وكشف الغطاء عن مشكلاتها مبلغا يرجع معه الحق باهر
الرواء، ظاهر في السناء.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Weakness, feebleness of structure or constitution; opposite of strength (quwwa).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used of arguments whose premises lack demonstrative force; epistemic frailty.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for bodily weakness; metaphorical (majāz) for the infirmity of rational proofs.
- Root: ق-ل-د (q-l-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To wind a necklace around the neck; to imitate blindly.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taqlīd — acceptance of doctrine without evidence; the antithesis of naẓar (rational inquiry).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: placing a garland; metaphorical: following authority without verification.
- Root: ع-ل-ق (ʿ-l-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To hang, suspend, attach; relation of attachment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taʿalluq — the soul-body relation in philosophical psychology; the mode of connection between two entities.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: hanging a thing from another; metaphorical: the relation of governance (tadbīr) between soul and body.
- Root: خ-ر-ق (kh-r-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To tear, rend, pierce; to break through.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Kharq al-ʿādah — the breaking of customary natural patterns; miracle as supernatural intervention.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: tearing a garment; metaphorical: violating the habitual course of nature.
- Sībawayh Rule: Al-Ḥāl and the Conditional Clause (Jumla Sharṭiyya) — The sentence "If they made it a matter of qiyās, they err" employs the conditional construction where the protasis (condition) is followed by the apodosis (result), governing the logical structure of refutation.
chapters.translation:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate — and in Him is my trust.

To proceed: After praise of God, and prayer upon Muhammad, the best of His creation, and upon his family — I have observed that the inquiries of the Christians concerning their doctrines are weak in foundation, feeble in force, and rugged in path. The contemplative mind that inclines toward them is driven to the utmost astonishment, and one does not attain from their complexity even the slightest of one's need. They rely in these matters upon nothing but pure taqlīd (blind acceptance), clinging with their molar teeth to the outward expressions (ẓawāhir) that the earlier ones uttered, while the later ones — due to their deficiency — did not rise to clarifying what is problematic therein. They suppose that this is the sacred law (sharʿ) that Jesus, peace be upon him, legislated for them, excusing their belief by what has come down of texts that they deem to be compelling against unbelief, not susceptible to interpretation (taʾwīl), and that diverting them from their outward senses is difficult.

In this matter, they are two sects:

- A sect — and they are the majority — who have not practiced any of the sciences by which the inquirer comes to know the impossibility of the impossible, so as to judge with certainty the impossibility of its existence; nor the necessitation of the Necessary, so as to negate the non-occurrence of what must be; nor the possibility of the possible, so that no impossibility is entailed by either side of its existence or non-existence. Rather, images have been imprinted in their minds since their youth, and obtuseness has persisted with them until this became a fixed disposition (malaka) in them. This sect — curing them of their malady is difficult.

- And a sect who possess the least degree of rationality, having touched upon a small measure of the sciences. You find them recoiling from this belief, not permitting their thoughts to approach it. They rely at times upon the taqlīd of the philosopher in the question of union (ittiḥād), due to their veneration of what it leads to in demolishing the foundations whose establishment the clear dictates of the intellects (ṣarāʾiḥ al-ʿuqūl) have mutually supported. They flee from this dilemma to pure taqlīd, believing that the philosopher has attempted the hidden sciences and rendered them clear and demonstrated. They suppose that one whose state is such is worthy of reliance upon his statements and of being followed in beliefs! Therefore, they extricate themselves from the question of union (ittiḥād) by referring it to the question of the soul's attachment (taʿalluq) to the body.

Were these wretched ones to consult their intellects and abandon caprice and partisanship, they would know that they have deviated from the highway of correctness and missed the path of truth, for several reasons:

One of them: If they make this a matter of qiyās (analogical reasoning), they err — because qiyās is: "the referring of a branch (farʿ) to a root (aṣl) by a uniting cause (ʿilla) that is the basis of the judgment (manāṭ al-ḥukm)."

And what cause has this speaker comprehended that would necessitate the reality of the attachment (taʿalluq) that the philosopher affirms, and then, after that, he extends it to the Essence of the Creator (dhāt al-Bārī) so that the qiyās might be valid for him?

And if they make it a matter of comparison and analogy (tashbīh wa-tamthīl), they also err — because the thing compared to (al-mushabbah bihī) must be known and conceived, so that knowledge of it necessitates knowledge of the similarity. And the one among them who holds this doctrine — were he to exert his utmost effort to produce the slightest doubt that would acquaint him with the reality of the soul and the reality of the attachment that the philosopher affirms — he would confess his incapacity to grasp that. So how can qiyās be valid for him when the realities are unknown to him?!

Moreover, such a qiyās is not permitted even to the practitioner of furūʿ (branches of jurisprudence) himself in its use; rather, it is among the abandoned analogies (al-aqyisa al-mahjūra), called qiyās al-taʿqīd (the analogy of complication) — namely, that one attempts to establish a hidden judgment, then establishes it by what is even more hidden than it, or by what requires, in its establishment, the exertion of thought and its extraction through obscure proofs — like the soul that the philosopher affirms, whose existence is not imagined except through complications and obscurity in its derivation. And if this is abandoned in the branches (furūʿ) built upon the slightest conjecture, how can one rely upon it in the principles (uṣūl) pertaining to the Essence of the Necessary Existent (wājib al-wujūd)?! And how can that claim be completed, when the basis of the judgment (manāṭ al-ḥukm) — even if it were stumbled upon — would require that the deity have no attachment to the essence of any human being in the manner of the soul's attachment to the body? For they say: Every soul that has attached itself to a body — the condition of its attachment is that there be between them a suitability and congruity (munāsaba wa-mulāʾama) for the sake of which the attachment occurred. And God — exalted be His name — is transcendent above anything of that sort.

Then, even if this were granted to them — that the attachment they attempted is conceivable in accordance with the philosophical opinions — they would gain no benefit from it, nor would it advance their purpose in establishing the divinity of Jesus, peace be upon him.

For the philosopher says: The soul has a governing attachment (taʿalluq tadbīrī) to the body, and that pleasure and pain occur to both by means of its attachment to it, when the sensitive faculty is affected by what is agreeable or repugnant. And it is impossible that this attachment in its entirety, along with what has been mentioned, be intended — because the occurrence of pleasures to the Essence of the Creator is impossible.

It remains that this governing relation (al-nisba al-tadbīriyya) be taken in abstraction from the occurrence of pleasures — and this too is of no avail, because the Creator is the governor (mudabbir) of every individual of the world, and to Him belongs a governing relation to every creature.

If it is said: What is meant is a relation whose effect has appeared in the breaking of customs (kharq al-ʿawāʾid) — like the reviving of the dead and other such things — then that would indicate the intended purpose.

The answer: Such a relation — by which the one characterized by it is able to perform the breaking of customs — is established for other than Jesus, peace be upon him. For they acknowledge that Moses, peace be upon him, turned the staff into a serpent.

And is the reviving of the dead anything other than the description of an inanimate thing with animality? Rather, this is more indicative of the miracle — because making what has never been characterized by life at all into a living thing is more indicative of power than restoring a thing to its former state. Then the splitting of the sea and the making of each part like a mighty mountain — these are among the wonders of miracles.

And the Torah, which they affirm as true, has testified that Moses, peace be upon him, brought forth his hand white like snow, then returned it to the color of his body.

And in the books of Kings and Judges — which are among their ancient books read in their churches — that Elijah and Elisha his disciple raised the dead. And Elijah's reviving of the widow's son is not denied among them. And the standing still of the sun for Joshua until he took the city of Jericho — these are among the marvels of miracles.

Then, how many of the prophets were prophets not sent [with a mission]? So what prevents that this relation be established for each one of them, but it did not appear due to the absence of a mission requiring the proofs issuing from it?!

A subtle point that must be noted:

The wording of the Mighty Book: {«Wa-ḍmum yadaka ilā janāḥika takhruj bayḍāʾa min ghayri sūʾ»} — "And draw your hand to your side; it will come out white without harm" (Q. 20:22). And the wording of the Torah: "Here, O you who forms, white like snow."

And the interpretation of this Hebrew expression into Arabic: "And this is your hand, leprous like snow."

The Torah explicitly stated leprosy (baraṣ), while the explicit wording of the Mighty Book states that its whiteness was "without harm" (min ghayri sūʾ). And in the heart there is a prickling of doubt about this at first glance — but the reconciliation is not difficult for the practiced and understanding one.

Its explanation: Leprosy (baraṣ) is an expression for an accident arising from a corrupted temperament (sūʾ al-mizāj), by which occurs a viscosity of phlegm that the transforming faculty (al-quwwa al-mughayyira) is too weak to convert into the color of the body. And it is known that the whiteness of Moses' hand, peace be upon him, did not arise from a corrupted temperament — because if anyone's temperament were corrupted in the manner we have described, that would occur to him; and if the transforming faculty were strengthened to convert it, then the specificity of the miracle would disappear. Rather, its whiteness was of the kind of the miraculous breaking of custom (al-muʿjiz al-khāriq). And the nature of the miraculous breaking of custom is that it be contrary to the accustomed and familiar. And to this meaning the Mighty Book alludes in His saying: "without harm" (min ghayri sūʾ) — that is, God empowered Moses to make his hand leprous without harm, and to return it to the color of his body, without a transforming faculty — so that thereby there accrues to him a specificity in the performance of the miraculous breaking of custom that is contrary to the accustomed, upon his hand.

And it is only a miracle contrary to the accustomed when one brings about the effect (al-musabbab) disjoined from its customary cause, which does not arise except from it — then expresses it by the whiteness that is among its necessary concomitants. This is a clear reconciliation.

And among what weakens their beliefs in this matter: The philosopher's principle concerning the soul and its attachment — if they are certain of its establishment, and the basis of their certainty is a good opinion of those who affirm it, while they are unable to produce its proofs — supposing that those who affirm it have invented from the hidden sciences what thought recoils from grasping, due to the obscurity of its derivation and the difficulty of its foundations. And that one whose state is such — his statements are to be deemed free from error. Then it is incumbent upon this speaker to practice taqlīd of the philosopher in that prophecies are acquired (muktasaba), that the world is eternal (qadīm) not admitting of origination and corruption (kawn wa-fasād), that the Creator does not know particulars (juzʾiyyāt), that from the One only one proceeds, that the deity of creation is a bare existence (wujūd mujarrad) with no knowledge, life, or power subsisting in His Essence — and other such things by which they have demolished the foundations of the followers of the sacred law and in which they have explicitly declared the prophets, the messengers, to be liars.

And it is a wonder that they practice taqlīd of a people who deny the conceivability of that by which the specificity of the founder of their law is established — for they explicitly state the impossibility of the formation of a child from the mere semen of his mother without the participation of a man's semen — either coagulating according to the opinion of their chief, or participating in the partiality according to the opinion of Galen.

If a speaker, driven by his partisanship and his caprice that incite him not to abandon what he has habituated, says: "What has been mentioned — the proofs have established their error in it — so they remain, in what is beyond it, upon the requirement of our opinion of them."

The answer: Whoever has appeared at times erroneous and at times correct — his statements are possible of error and correctness. And one does not resort to taqlīd of one whose state is such, in the absence of grasping the basis of his statements — while casting the statements of the followers of the sacred law behind one's back, and not deigning to rely upon the outward senses of his Book that indicate the humanity of the founder of his law — except for texts that refuse interpretation, indicating what they claim of divinity, resistant to the intellects with an evident resistance. How so, when in the Gospel there are texts explicitly stating the pure humanity of Jesus, peace be upon him, and texts witnessing that the application of divinity to him, as they claim, is impossible?

And these texts are in the most authentic of the Gospels according to them: the Gospel of John son of Zebedee.

And behold, I shall mention them text by text, clarifying the chapters inscribed therein, as a precaution against denial — because their books are not preserved in their breasts.

And before commencing their mention, it is necessary to present two principles agreed upon among the people of knowledge:

One of them: That when texts are presented — if they accord with the rational (al-maʿqūl), their outward senses are left as they are; and if they contradict the clear rational (ṣarīḥ al-maʿqūl), their interpretation (taʾwīl) is obligatory, and one must believe that their realities are not intended — in which case they must be referred to metaphor (majāz).

The second: That when evidences are mutually contradictory — some indicating the establishment of a judgment and some indicating its negation — we do not leave them in contradiction except when we have sensed from ourselves incapacity due to the impossibility of reconciliation and the prevention of making them mutually supportive upon a single meaning.

And when that is established, let us now commence the mention of the texts indicating the figurative usage (tajawwuz) in his application to himself of what suggests divinity.

And the texts indicating the figurative usage in the question of union (ittiḥād) — such as his saying:

"I and the Father are one, and whoever has seen me has seen the Father, and I am in the Father, and the Father is in me."

Then we shall follow that with the mention of the texts indicating his pure humanity, and we shall reconcile between them and the texts that stirred for them doubts — their understandings having recoiled due to their deficiency from interpreting them — so they became blind and went astray. We shall be exhaustive in clarifying them and uncovering the veil from their difficulties, to a degree with which the truth returns resplendent in appearance, manifest in luminosity.

chapters.title_en: The Elegant Refutation of the Divinity of Jesus through the Plain Text of the Gospel — Section 2: On the Two Johannine Passages Concerning Union (ittiḥād) and Their Metaphorical Interpretation
chapters.arabic_text:
### | AUTO النص الأول:

ذكره يوحنا في إنجيله في الفصل الرابع والعشرين:
«أنا والأب واحد، فتناول اليهود حجارة ليرجموه، فأجابهم قائلا:
أريتكم أعمالا كثيرة حسنة من عند أبي، من أجل أي الأعمال ترجموني؟
فأجابه اليهود قائلين: ليس من أجل الأعمال الحسنة نرجمك، ولكن لأجل
التجديف، وإذ أنت إنسان تجعل نفسك إلها.
فأجابهم يسوع: أليس مكتوبا في ناموسكم أني قلت إنكم آلهة، فإن كان قد
قال/ لأولئك آلهة لأن الكلمة صارت إليهم، وليس يمكن أن ينتقص المكتوب فيكم
بالحرا الذي قدسه وأرسله إلى العالم» «2».
هذا آخر كلامه.
فنقول: هذا النص بالغ في تحصيل غرضنا الذي نحاوله في مسألة الاتحاد،
وبيانه: أن اليهود لما أنكروا عليه قوله: «أنا والأب واحد». وهذه هي مسألة
الاتحاد نفسها. ظانين بأنه أراد بقوله: «أنا والأب واحد»؛ مفهومه الظاهر،
فيكون إلها حقيقة، انفصل عليه السلام عن إنكارهم، مصرحا بأن ذلك من قبيل
المجاز، ثم  أبان لهم جهة التجوز بضربه لهم المثل/ فقال: «قد أطلق عليكم في
ناموسكم أنكم آلهة، ولستم آلهة حقيقة» وإنما أطلق عليكم هذا اللفظ لمعنى،
وهو: صيرورة الكلمة إليكم، وأنا قد شاركتكم في ذلك.
PageV01P038
وقد ورد مثل ذلك في شريعتنا، قال سيد المسلمين صلى الله عليه وسلم حاكيا عن
الحق جل اسمه: «ولن يتقرب إلي المتقربون بأفضل من أداء ما افترضت عليهم، ثم
لا يزال العبد يتقرب إلي بالنوافل حتى أحبه، فإذا أحببته، كنت سمعه الذي
يسمع به، وبصره الذي يبصر به، ولسانه الذي ينطق به، ويده الذي يبطش بها» «1».
ومحال أن يكون الخالق حالا/ في كل جارحة من هذه الجوارح، أو يكون عبارة عنها.
لكن لما بذل العبد جهده في طاعة الله، كان له من الله قدرة ومعونة، بهما
يقدر على النطق باللسان، والبطش باليد، إلى غير ذلك من الأعمال المقربة «2».
ولذلك يقول من أقدر شخصا على أن يضرب بالسيف؛ ولو لاه لما قدر على ذلك:
أنا يدك التي ضربت بها.
فهذا ضرب من المجاز، استعماله حسن شائع غير منكور، وقد صرح عيسى- عليه
السلام- في هذا النص بجهة المجاز، بقوله: «لأن الكلمة صارت إليهم». ومحال
أن يريد بالكلمة لفظا ذا حروف، وإنما يريد/ بالكلمة؛ سرا منه يهبه لمن يشاء
من عباده، يحصل لهم به التوفيق إلى ما يصيرهم غير مباينين لله عز وجل، بل
يصيرهم لا يحبون إلا ما يحبه، ولا PageV01P039
يبغضون إلا ما يبغضه، ولا يكرهون إلا ما يكرهه، ولا يريدون إلا ما يريده من
الأقوال والأعمال اللائقة بجلاله.
فإذا أصارهم التوفيق إلى هذه الحالة، حصل لهم المعنى المصحح للتجوز. ويدل
على صحة هذا التأويل الصارف إلى المجاز المذكور، أنه عليه السلام، احترز عن
إرادة ظاهر هذا النص الدال على الاتحاد، بقوله:
«فيكم بالحرا الذي قدسه وأرسله». فصرح بأنه رسول متبرئا من الإلهية/ التي
تخيل اليهود أنه ادعاها مثبتا لنفسه خصوصية الأنبياء، وعلو درجاتهم على
غيرهم ممن ليسوا أنبياء، بقوله: «فيكم الحر الذي قدسه وأرسله»، أي قد
شاركتكم في السبب  المصحح للتجوز، وفضلتكم بمراتب النبوة والرسالة.
ولو لم يكن ما ضربه لهم من التمثيل جوابا قاطعا لما تخيلوه من إرادة ظاهر
اللفظ، لكان ذلك مغالطة منه وغشا في المعتقدات المفضي الجهل بها إلى سخط
الإله، وهذا لا يليق بالأنبياء المرسلين الهادين إلى الحق. لأن تأخير
البيان عن وقت الحاجة/، غير جائز للأنبياء، كيف وفي كتبهم أنه أرسل لخلاص
العالم، مبينا ما يجب لله وما يستحيل عليه؟!
وإنما يكون مخلصا للعالم إذا بين لهم الإله المعبود، فإن كان هو الإله
الذي يجب أن يعبد، وقد صرفهم عن اعتقاد ذلك بضربه لهم المثل، فيكون قد
أمرهم بعبادة غيره، وصرفهم عن عبادته، والتقدير أنه هو الإله الذي يجب أن
يعبد، وذلك غش وضلالة، لا يليق بمن يدعى فيه أنه أتى لخلاص العالم، بل لا
يليق بمن انتصب للإرشاد والهداية من آحاد الأمم، فضلا عمن صرح بأنه رسول
هاد/ مرشد.
فإن قيل: إنما ضرب لم المثل؛ مغالطة ليدفع عن نفسه ما يحذره من شرهم.
قلنا: الخوف من اليهود لا يليق بمن يدعى فيه أنه إله العالم، وموجد
الكائنات!!
فليت شعري، ما ذا يقول المعاند بعد أن لاحت له هذه الحقائق أوضح من فرق
الصبح؟ وكيف يتقاعد عن تأويل هذا النص وتأويل أمثاله، ويخبط خبط عشواء،
وصاحب شريعته قد أوله نفسه «1»؟!
PageV01P040

### | AUTO النص الثاني:

نص عليه يوحنا المذكور في إنجيله، وفي الفصل السابع والثلاثين:
«أيها الأب القدوس احفظهم/ باسمك الذي أعطيتني، ليكونوا معك واحدا، كما
نحن» «1».
هذا النص كالنص الذي قبله سواء، مؤكدا «2» في صرفه عن الحقيقة إلى المجاز
المذكور، وبيانه: أنه عليه السلام، دعا الله عز وجل لتلامذته أن يكون حافظا
لهم باسمه حفظا مثل حفظه له، ليحصل لهم بذلك الحفظ وحدة بالله، ثم أتى بحرف
التشبيه، فقال: «كما نحن»؛ أي: تكون تلك الوحدة كوحدتي معك، فإن تكن وحدته
مع الإله موجبة له استحقاق الإلهية، فيلزم أن يكون داعيا لتلامذته/ أن
يكونوا آلهة.
وخطور ذلك ببال من خلع ربقة العقل، قبيح، فضلا عن من  يكون له أدنى خيال
صحيح، بل هذا محمول على المجاز المذكور، وهو أنه عليه السلام سأل الله أن
يفيض عليهم من آلائه وعنايته وتوفيقه إلى ما يرشدهم إلى مراده اللائق
بجلاله، بحيث لا يريدون إلا ما يريده، ولا يحبون إلا ما يحبه، ولا يبغضون
إلا ما يبغضه، ولا يكرهون إلا ما يكرهه، ولا يأتون من الأقوال والأعمال إلا
ما هو راض به، مؤثر لوقوعه، فإذا حصلت لهم/ هذه الحالة حسن التجوز. ويدل
على صحة ذلك، أن إنسانا لو كان له صديق موافق غرضه ومراده بحيث يكون محبا
لما يحبه، مبغضا لما يبغضه، كارها لما يكرهه، حسن أن يقول: أنا وصديقي واحد.
وقد بين عليه السلام أيضا في النص أن وحدته معه مجاز، وأنه ليس إلها
حقيقة بقوله: «ليكونوا معك واحدا كما نحن» يريد: إذا حصل لهم منك توفيق،
صيرهم لا يريدون إلا ما تريده، كانت وحدتهم معك كوحدتي معك، إذ هذه حالتي
معك لأنني لا أريد إلا ما تريده/، ولا أحب إلا ما تحبه. وبقوله أيضا: «أيها
الأب القدوس احفظهم باسمك». داعيا لهم الإله PageV01P041
الذي بيده النفع والضر، ولو كان نفسه إلها، لكان قادرا على حفظهم من غير أن
يتضرع لغيره ويسأله الحفظ.
فاعجب لهذه الإشارات التي نبه بها على إرادة المجاز، وصرف الكلام عن ظاهره.
وقد صرح بولص «1» في رسالته التي سيرها إلى قورنتية «2»؛ بمثل ذلك، لما
فهم المراد من هذه النصوص، فقال: «فمن اعتصم بربنا فإنه يكون معه روحا
واحدا» «3». وهذا التصريح منه يدل على أنه فهم عين ما فهمناه «4» /، وفهم
أن هذه النصوص، ليست ظواهرها مرادة.

- Root: و-ح-د (w-ḥ-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Oneness, unity, singularity; the state of being one (wāḥid) without composition or multiplicity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, al-waḥdah denotes the absolute simplicity of the Divine Essence, which admits no partner, division, or incarnation (ḥulūl). When applied to creatures, it is purely relational and metaphorical.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) unity is exclusive to God; any attribution of unity between Creator and creature is a recognized metaphor (majāz) of concordance and submission, not ontological identity.
- Root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Speech, word, utterance; the act of addressing (taklīm). In the Gospel citation, "the Word" (al-kalimah) is not a phonetic utterance but a divine bestowal.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Kalām Allāh is an eternal attribute; when "the word comes to" prophets, it signifies revelation and divine favor, not hypostatic union.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The phrase "the Word became to them" is majāz — a metaphor for the indwelling of divine guidance and grace, not a literal descent of the Divine into a human nature.
- Root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To settle, dwell, descend into a place; indwelling (ḥulūl).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ḥulūl is categorically impossible for God in the sense of spatial or substantial inherence; the term is used only to refute the Christian claim of incarnation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The metaphorical use of "God becomes one's hearing and sight" (in the ḥadīth) is a figure of divine empowerment, not a literal indwelling.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Taʾwīl (Interpretive Redirection) — When a literal reading (ẓāhir) entails impossibility (muḥāl) or blasphemy, the sentence is parsed as majāz, with the grammatical subject (musnad ilayh) redirected to a permissible sense, as in "You are gods" (antum ālihah) — a predicate of honor, not essence.
chapters.translation:
I say — and with God is the success:

**The First Text:**

John mentioned it in his Gospel, in the twenty-fourth chapter: «I and the Father are one. So the Jews took up stones to stone him. But he answered them, saying: 'Many good works have I shown you from my Father; for which of those works do you stone me?' The Jews answered him, saying: 'We do not stone you for a good work, but for blasphemy, and because you, being a man, make yourself God.' Jesus answered them: 'Is it not written in your law, I said, you are gods? If he called them gods, to whom the word of God came — and the scripture cannot be broken — do you say of him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, "You blaspheme"?'» This is the end of his speech.

We say: This text is most conclusive in achieving our very purpose concerning the question of union (ittiḥād). Its elucidation is this: When the Jews denied his saying, «I and the Father are one» — and this is the very question of union — supposing that he meant by his saying «I and the Father are one» its apparent sense, so that he would be truly God, he — peace be upon him — dissociated himself from their denial, explicitly declaring that this belongs to the category of metaphor (majāz). Then he showed them the aspect of the metaphorical usage by striking for them the parable, saying: «It has been said of you in your law that you are gods, and you are not gods in truth; rather, this expression was applied to you only for a certain meaning, namely, the coming of the Word to you, and I have shared with you in that.»

Page V01P038

And similar to this has occurred in our own sacred Law. The Master of the Muslims — may God bless him and grant him peace — said, narrating from the Truth — exalted be His Name: «The servants shall not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than the performance of what I have made obligatory upon them. Then the servant continues to draw near to Me with supererogatory acts until I love him; and when I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his tongue with which he speaks, and his hand with which he strikes.» Now it is impossible that the Creator should be an indwelling (ḥāll) in every one of these limbs, or that He should be an expression for them. Rather, when the servant expends his utmost effort in obedience to God, there is for him from God a power and an assistance (maʿūnah) by which he is enabled to speak with the tongue, to strike with the hand, and to perform other acts that bring him near.

For this reason, one who empowers another to strike with a sword — such that were it not for him, he would not be able to do it — says: "I am the hand with which you struck." This is a kind of metaphor whose usage is good, widespread, and not disapproved. And Jesus — peace be upon him — explicitly declared in this text the aspect of the metaphor by his saying: «because the Word came to them.» It is impossible that he meant by "the Word" a phonetic utterance composed of letters. Rather, he meant by "the Word" a secret from Him which He bestows upon whomsoever He wills of His servants, by which there is obtained for them the divine success (tawfīq) that renders them not separate from God — mighty and majestic is He — but rather renders them such that they love nothing but what He loves, and hate nothing but what He hates, and dislike nothing but what He dislikes, and will nothing but what He wills of the sayings and deeds befitting His majesty.

When divine success brings them to this state, there is obtained for them the meaning that validates the metaphorical usage. And that which indicates the soundness of this interpretation — which diverts to the aforementioned metaphor — is that he — peace be upon him — guarded against intending the apparent sense of this text that indicates union, by his saying: «whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world.» For he explicitly declared himself a messenger, disavowing the divinity that the Jews imagined he had claimed, while affirming for himself the particular distinction of the prophets and the elevation of their ranks above others who are not prophets, by his saying: «whom the Father sanctified and sent» — that is, "I have shared with you in the cause that validates the metaphor, and I have been preferred above you by the ranks of prophethood and messengership."

Had the parable he struck for them not been a decisive answer to what they had imagined of his intending the apparent sense of the expression, that would have been a sophistry on his part and a deception in matters of belief, ignorance of which leads to the wrath of the Divine — and this is not befitting the sent prophets who guide to the truth. For the postponement of clarification beyond the time of need is not permissible for prophets. How could it be, when in their books it is [written] that he was sent for the salvation of the world, clarifying what is obligatory for God and what is impossible for Him?!

And he would only be a savior of the world if he clarified for them the worshipped God. For if he himself were the God who must be worshipped, and he diverted them from believing that by striking for them the parable, then he would have commanded them to worship another, and diverted them from worshipping him — and the supposition is that he is the God who must be worshipped. That would be deception and error, not befitting one of whom it is claimed that he came for the salvation of the world — nay, not befitting any single individual among the nations who undertakes guidance and direction, let alone one who explicitly declared himself a messenger, a guide, a director.

If it is said: "He only struck the parable as a sophistry to repel from himself the evil he feared from them," we say: Fear of the Jews is not befitting one of whom it is claimed that he is the God of the world and the Originator of all created things!!

Would that I knew — what would the obstinate one say after these truths have become manifest to him clearer than the splitting of dawn? And how could he hold back from interpreting this text and others like it, and flounder about blindly, when the founder of his own law has himself interpreted it?!

Page V01P040

**The Second Text:**

The aforementioned John stated it in his Gospel, in the thirty-seventh chapter: «Holy Father, keep them in your name which you have given me, that they may be one with you, even as we are one.»

This text is exactly like the one before it, even more emphatic in diverting it from the literal to the aforementioned metaphorical sense. Its elucidation: He — peace be upon him — prayed to God — mighty and majestic — for his disciples that He would be a keeper for them in His name, a keeping like His keeping of him, so that there might be obtained for them by that keeping a unity with God. Then he brought the particle of comparison (ḥarf al-tashbīh) and said: «even as we are one» — that is, "let that unity be like my unity with You." For if his unity with the Divine necessitated for him the deserving of divinity, then it would follow that he was praying for his disciples to become gods.

And the mere occurrence of such a thought in the mind of one who has cast off the rein of reason is vile — let alone one who possesses the least sound imagination. Rather, this is to be borne upon the aforementioned metaphor, namely, that he — peace be upon him — asked God to pour out upon them from His bounties, His care, and His divine success that which would guide them to His will befitting His majesty, such that they would will nothing but what He wills, love nothing but what He loves, hate nothing but what He hates, dislike nothing but what He dislikes, and utter no sayings and perform no deeds but what He is pleased with and prefers to come to pass. When this state is obtained for them, the metaphorical usage becomes fitting. And that which indicates the soundness of this is that if a man had a friend who conformed to his purpose and will — such that he loves what he loves, hates what he hates, and dislikes what he dislikes — it would be proper for him to say: "I and my friend are one."

He — peace be upon him — also made clear in the text that his unity with Him is metaphorical, and that he is not truly God, by his saying: «that they may be one with you, even as we are one» — meaning: "When there is obtained for them from You a divine success that renders them willing nothing but what You will, their unity with You is like my unity with You, for this is my state with You, because I will nothing but what You will, and love nothing but what You love." And also by his saying: «Holy Father, keep them in your name» — for he was supplicating the Divine who holds in His hand benefit and harm. Had he himself been God, he would have been able to keep them without beseeching another and asking Him for their protection.

So marvel at these indications by which he alerted to his intending the metaphor, and diverted the speech from its apparent sense. And Paul has explicitly stated the like of this in his epistle which he sent to the Corinthians, when he understood the intended meaning of these texts, saying: «He who clings to our Lord shall be with Him one spirit.» This explicit statement of his indicates that he understood exactly what we have understood, and understood that the apparent senses of these texts are not what is intended.
